On 2 October 2023, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2699 by 13 votes to none, with China and Russia abstaining. Ecuador and the United States sponsored the draft resolution. Acting under Chapter VII, the Council authorized participating Member States to form and deploy the Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission in Haiti, designating a lead country and coordinating with Haitian authorities. The authorization covers a 12-month period, subject to a review after nine months, with financing through voluntary contributions. The mission's mandate supports Haitian police efforts to restore security and create conditions for free and fair elections. The Council mandated a human rights compliance mechanism for participating States and required the mission to establish oversight. Furthermore, the Council requested that mission leaders report to the Secretary-General every three months once operational.

No national source cards were provided; therefore, no specific rationales, claims, or differing positions from the delegations are recorded in this record. The abstentions by China and Russia are noted as part of the voting tally but do not include attributed views due to the absence of supporting documentation. The Council's legal authority to act under Chapter VII is distinct from the unattributed positions of the abstaining members. The resolution carries the full legal force of a Security Council decision under the UN Charter.
